title: Modus ponens
hint: Cite the implication and its antecedent with ImpE.

title: A conjunction can be turned around
hint: Take the conjunction apart with AndE, then put it back together the other way round with AndI.

title: Adding a disjunct
hint: OrI needs only one side of the disjunction; the other side can be any formula.

title: Following two implications
hint: Use ImpE twice: first on P → Q, then on Q → R.

title: Anything follows from a contradiction
hint: NotE turns P and ¬P into ⊥, and BotE turns ⊥ into anything.

title: P implies P
hint: Open a subproof that assumes P, and close it straight away with ImpI 1-1.

title: Chaining implications
hint: Assume P inside a subproof, get R with two uses of ImpE, then close the subproof with ImpI.

title: Introducing a double negation
hint: To prove ¬¬P, assume ¬P and reach ⊥. NotI then gives ¬¬P.

title: Modus tollens
hint: Assume P, derive Q, and clash it with ¬Q to get ⊥. NotI closes the subproof.

title: A disjunction can be turned around
hint: Use OrE: one subproof for each side of P ∨ Q, each ending in Q ∨ P.

title: Contraposition
hint: Assume ¬Q, and inside that assume P. Derive ⊥, close with NotI, then close the outer subproof with ImpI.

title: Disjunctive syllogism
hint: Use OrE. In the P case, P clashes with ¬P, so BotE gives anything. In the Q case you already have Q.

title: De Morgan: not (P or Q)
hint: Prove ¬P and ¬Q separately. Each needs a subproof that assumes the formula and reaches ⊥ using the premise. Join them with AndI.

title: P and Q is equivalent to Q and P
hint: IffI needs two subproofs: one assuming P ∧ Q and ending in Q ∧ P, and one going the other way.

title: The law of excluded middle
hint: Assume ¬(P ∨ ¬P) and show that leads to ⊥. Then NotI gives ¬¬(P ∨ ¬P) and DNE finishes the proof.
